title: Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements: Conditions of Enrollment and Activation
content:
**Rule.** The customer's customer type must be one of the customer types in the entry gate of the tier applied for, and the properties listed may not exceed the tier's maximum sites. A customer whose agreement of the same tier expired or was cancelled may enroll again at that tier only after the tier's re-enrollment wait has passed. The agreement must be in applied status when it is activated or withdrawn. An enrollment is reviewed within the tier's review business days and offered for signature; the customer's signature activates the agreement and starts a term of the tier's length, and the first term's fee is charged at activation. On tiers that require it, the first term's fee is paid before activation. An unsigned enrollment is withdrawn after the tier's application expiry days.

These conditions govern every enrollment in the Commercial & Property Manager Service Agreements, from submission through signature or withdrawal.

## Conditions, one by one

1. **Customer type and property count (at enrollment).** The customer type on the customer's own record must be one of the customer types in the entry gate of the tier applied for, and the number of properties listed on the enrollment may not exceed that tier's maximum sites. Both are read from the company's records for that customer, not from the customer's description.
2. **Re-enrollment wait (at enrollment).** Where the customer's records show an agreement of the same tier that expired or was cancelled, the customer may enroll again at that tier only after the tier's re-enrollment wait has passed. The wait is a number of calendar days after that agreement's expiry or cancellation, as recorded on that agreement, and it concerns enrollment again at the same tier as the expired or cancelled agreement.
3. **Status (at activation or withdrawal).** The agreement must be in applied status when it is activated or withdrawn; the status is the one on that agreement's record.
4. **Review and signature.** An enrollment is reviewed within the tier's review business days and offered for signature. The customer's signature activates the agreement and starts a term of the tier's length, and the first term's fee is charged at activation.
5. **Fee before activation.** On tiers that require it, the first term's fee is paid before activation.
6. **Lapse.** An unsigned enrollment is withdrawn after the tier's application expiry days.

A new enrollment opens in applied status with an agreement balance of 0.00. From applied status the agreement either becomes active when the customer signs, or becomes cancelled when the unsigned enrollment is withdrawn or lapses.

## Necessary conditions at a glance

| Moment | Condition | When the condition is not met |
|---|---|---|
| Enrollment | customer type in the tier's entry gate | the customer may not enroll at that tier |
| Enrollment | properties listed within the tier's maximum sites | the enrollment may not list that many properties at that tier |
| Enrollment | same-tier re-enrollment wait has passed | the customer may not yet enroll again at that tier |
| Activation or withdrawal | agreement in applied status | the agreement is not activated or withdrawn |
| Activation, on tiers that require it | first term's fee paid | the agreement is not activated before that payment |

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical figures)

- **Property count.** For a tier with a hypothetical maximum of 10 sites, an enrollment listing 11 properties exceeds the maximum; one listing 10 does not.
- **Re-enrollment wait.** For a tier with a hypothetical 30-day re-enrollment wait, an enrollment at that tier 12 calendar days after the earlier same-tier agreement expired falls inside the wait; one made 40 calendar days after the expiry falls after the wait has passed.
- **Status.** An agreement whose record already shows active status is not in applied status, so it is neither activated nor withdrawn under these conditions.
